assertions.text: The impact of the break on the work-optional date is stated as a range or under more than one named scenario, not as a single revised date.
Outcomes are reported under at least two different investment-return assumptions, one materially more conservative than the base case.

Statutory or regulatory figures quoted in the document (tax brackets or deductions, contribution limits, subsidy or poverty-line thresholds, penalty rules) each carry a source and the date they were checked.
The document names which accounts fund the break and in what order.
The funding plan either avoids early-withdrawal penalties on retirement accounts or, where a penalized withdrawal is contemplated, states the penalty and tax cost explicitly.
Health coverage is priced for all 24 months of the break; no part of the break period is left with unpriced or unspecified coverage.
The document evaluates using the low-income break years for Roth conversion or capital-gains harvesting, reaching a stated recommendation (doing either, or explicitly not, with a reason).
The document connects the size or source of withdrawals and conversions during the break to health-insurance subsidy eligibility (income thresholds), rather than treating the two as independent.
The planning horizon extends to at least age 95.

Downside outcomes are described in terms of what Maya would actually live on or do differently (spending level, break shortened, working longer), not solely as a portfolio survival or success percentage.
The document states at least one if-then rule with a numeric trigger and a defined checkpoint for delaying departure or cutting the break short.
The document shows the effect on the plan of re-entering work later than planned or at lower pay than the base assumption.
The asset figures the document is built on agree, within rounding, with the balances in Maya's own records.
The document names at least one specific item for Maya to verify with a licensed professional or the relevant official body — beyond a generic advice disclaimer.
The document names which money pays Maya's living costs if the post-break job search runs longer than planned.
